title: Impact of Bond Downgrade on Equity CAR

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event Study (market model). We measure abnormal returns (AR) as the difference between actual stock returns and expected returns given market movements, then cumulate AR over a short event window to obtain CAR. This isolates the immediate equity market reaction to a bond rating downgrade.
- Rationale: Downgrades are discrete, dated events. A short window around the announcement allows us to attribute price changes to the event under standard market efficiency assumptions.
- Key assumptions:
  - Correctly specified normal return model in the short window (stable alpha/beta; market model adequate).
  - No confounding firm-specific news precisely at the event that would systematically bias AR.
  - No leakage or anticipatory trading beyond the narrow window (tested via pre-event AR near zero).
  - Markets react quickly (semi-strong efficiency), so immediate CAR captures the causal effect.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE, scipen = 99)

# 1) Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s56_data.csv")

# Basic sanity checks
stopifnot(all(c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta") %in% names(df)))
df <- df[complete.cases(df[, c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta")]), ]

# 2) Compute abnormal returns using market model with given beta (alpha = 0)
df$AR_mkt <- df$ret - df$beta * df$mkt_ret

# Helper: compute CARs per stock for a given AR column and event-day set
compute_CARs <- function(data, ar_col, days_required) {
  stocks <- split(data, data$stock_id)
  cars <- c()
  ok_stocks <- c()
  for (sid in names(stocks)) {
    si <- stocks[[sid]]
    if (all(days_required %in% si$event_day)) {
      cars <- c(cars, sum(si[si$event_day %in% days_required, ar_col]))
      ok_stocks <- c(ok_stocks, sid)
    }
  }
  list(cars = cars, stocks = ok_stocks)
}

print_summary <- function(title, cars_vec) {
  n <- length(cars_vec)
  if (n == 0) {
    cat(title, ": No stocks with complete data for this window.\n", sep="")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  mean_car <- mean(cars_vec)
  sd_car <- sd(cars_vec)
  se_car <- sd_car / sqrt(n)
  t_stat <- ifelse(se_car > 0, mean_car / se_car, NA_real_)
  # 95% CI
  ci_lo <- mean_car - qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * se_car
  ci_hi <- mean_car + qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * se_car
  cat("\n", title, "\n", sep="")
  cat("  N stocks:", n, "\n")
  cat("  Mean CAR:", sprintf("%.4f", mean_car), "\n")
  cat("  t-stat  :", sprintf("%.2f", t_stat), "\n")
  cat("  95% CI  : [", sprintf("%.4f", ci_lo), ", ", sprintf("%.4f", ci_hi), "]\n", sep="")
}

# 3) Main estimates: immediate reaction windows
win_0      <- c(0)
win_01     <- c(0, 1)
win_m1_p1  <- c(-1, 0, 1)

res_0_mkt     <- compute_CARs(df, "AR_mkt", win_0)
res_01_mkt    <- compute_CARs(df, "AR_mkt", win_01)
res_m1p1_mkt  <- compute_CARs(df, "AR_mkt", win_m1_p1)

cat("Event Study: Impact of Bond Downgrade on Equity CAR (Market Model, beta given, alpha=0)\n")
print_summary("CAR[0,0] (Event day abnormal return)", res_0_mkt$cars)
print_summary("CAR[0,+1] (Immediate 2-day reaction)", res_01_mkt$cars)
print_summary("CAR[-1,+1] (Short 3-day reaction)", res_m1p1_mkt$cars)

# 4) Pre-trend / leakage check: mean pre-event AR in [-10,-2]
pre_window <- -10:-2
pre_ar_means <- c()
stocks <- split(df, df$stock_id)
for (sid in names(stocks)) {
  si <- stocks[[sid]]
  pre_si <- si[si$event_day %in% pre_window, ]
  if (nrow(pre_si) >= 3) {
    pre_ar_means <- c(pre_ar_means, mean(pre_si$AR_mkt))
  }
}
if (length(pre_ar_means) > 1) {
  n_pre <- length(pre_ar_means)
  mean_pre <- mean(pre_ar_means)
  sd_pre <- sd(pre_ar_means)
  se_pre <- sd_pre / sqrt(n_pre)
  t_pre <- ifelse(se_pre > 0, mean_pre / se_pre, NA_real_)
  ci_lo <- mean_pre - qt(0.975, df = n_pre - 1) * se_pre
  ci_hi <- mean_pre + qt(0.975, df = n_pre - 1) * se_pre
  cat("\nPre-event check (mean AR over [-10,-2])\n")
  cat("  N stocks:", n_pre, "\n")
  cat("  Mean pre-AR:", sprintf("%.5f", mean_pre), "\n")
  cat("  t-stat     :", sprintf("%.2f", t_pre), "\n")
  cat("  95% CI     : [", sprintf("%.5f", ci_lo), ", ", sprintf("%.5f", ci_hi), "]\n", sep="")
} else {
  cat("\nPre-event check: insufficient pre-event data across stocks.\n")
}

# 5) Robustness: Re-estimate alpha and beta from pre-event [-10,-1], then recompute AR and CARs
df$AR_ols <- NA_real_
stocks <- split(df, df$stock_id)
for (sid in names(stocks)) {
  si <- stocks[[sid]]
  est <- si[si$event_day <= -1 & si$event_day >= -10, ]
  if (nrow(est) >= 5) {
    fit <- try(lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = est), silent = TRUE)
    if (!inherits(fit, "try-error")) {
      pred <- predict(fit, newdata = si)
      df$AR_ols[df$stock_id == as.numeric(sid)] <- si$ret - pred
    }
  }
}

# Only use stocks with non-missing AR_ols in the required days
res_0_ols <- compute_CARs(df[!is.na(df$AR_ols), ], "AR_ols", win_0)
res_01_ols <- compute_CARs(df[!is.na(df$AR_ols), ], "AR_ols", win_01)
res_m1p1_ols <- compute_CARs(df[!is.na(df$AR_ols), ], "AR_ols", win_m1_p1)

cat("\nRobustness: Event Study using estimated alpha and beta from [-10,-1]\n")
print_summary("CAR[0,0] (Event day abnormal return, OLS est.)", res_0_ols$cars)
print_summary("CAR[0,+1] (Immediate 2-day reaction, OLS est.)", res_01_ols$cars)
print_summary("CAR[-1,+1] (Short 3-day reaction, OLS est.)", res_m1p1_ols$cars)

# 6) Additional robustness: test zero mean AR on event day 0 directly (cross-sectional)
#    under both models (where available)
# Market model (given beta)
ar0_mkt <- aggregate(AR_mkt ~ stock_id, data = df[df$event_day == 0, ], FUN = mean)
if (nrow(ar0_mkt) > 0) {
  m <- mean(ar0_mkt$AR_mkt); s <- sd(ar0_mkt$AR_mkt); n <- nrow(ar0_mkt); se <- s/sqrt(n)
  tstat <- ifelse(se > 0, m/se, NA_real_)
  cat("\nCross-sectional test: Mean AR on day 0 (market model)\n")
  cat("  N stocks:", n, "\n")
  cat("  Mean AR0:", sprintf("%.4f", m), "\n")
  cat("  t-stat  :", sprintf("%.2f", tstat), "\n")
}

# OLS model
ar0_ols <- aggregate(AR_ols ~ stock_id, data = df[!is.na(df$AR_ols) & df$event_day == 0, ], FUN = mean)
if (nrow(ar0_ols) > 0) {
  m <- mean(ar0_ols$AR_ols); s <- sd(ar0_ols$AR_ols); n <- nrow(ar0_ols); se <- s/sqrt(n)
  tstat <- ifelse(se > 0, m/se, NA_real_)
  cat("\nCross-sectional test: Mean AR on day 0 (OLS est.)\n")
  cat("  N stocks:", n, "\n")
  cat("  Mean AR0:", sprintf("%.4f", m), "\n")
  cat("  t-stat  :", sprintf("%.2f", tstat), "\n")
}

cat("\nNote: CAR values are in return units (e.g., -0.0150 equals -1.50%).\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. Downgrades typically depress equity prices due to higher expected distress costs, tighter financing, and worse cash flow prospects.
- Magnitude: For the immediate window, I expect:
  - CAR[0,0] around -0.5% to -1.5%.
  - CAR[0,+1] around -1.0% to -2.0%.
  - CAR[-1,+1] around -1.5% to -3.0%.
- The OLS-estimated model should yield similar magnitudes. Pre-event average AR should be near zero, supporting limited leakage.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare equity CAR before and after bond downgrades.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: A bond credit rating downgrade leads to a positive change in equity CAR.
